source_units.text: For David. By Babylon’s rivers, there we sat and wept when we remembered Zion.
Upon the willows in her midst we hung our instruments.
For there those who took us captive asked us for words of songs, and those who led us away for a hymn: “Sing us some of Zion’s songs.”
How can we sing the Lord’s song on foreign land?
If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand be forgotten.
May my tongue cling to my throat if I do not remember you, if I do not set Jerusalem first at the beginning of my gladness.
Remember, Lord, Edom’s sons on Jerusalem’s day, those saying, “Empty her, empty her, down to the foundation within her!”
Daughter Babylon, miserable one, happy is the one who will repay you the repayment you gave us.
Happy is the one who will seize your infants and dash them against the rock.
For David. I will thank Thee, Lord, with all my heart, for Thou heardest the words of my mouth, and before angels I will make music unto Thee.
I will bow toward Thy holy temple and thank Thy name for Thy mercy and Thy truth, for Thou hast magnified Thine utterance above every name.
On whatever day I call Thee, hear me quickly; Thou wilt greatly attend to me with strength in my soul.
Let all earth’s kings thank Thee, Lord, for they heard all the words of Thy mouth.
And let them sing in the Lord’s ways, for great is the Lord’s glory.
For the Lord is high and watches the lowly, and the lofty He knows from afar.
If I walk amid affliction, Thou wilt keep me alive; against my enemies’ anger Thou didst stretch out Thy hand, and Thy right hand saved me.
The Lord will repay on my behalf. Lord, Thy mercy is for ever; do not neglect the works of Thy hands.
For the end. A psalm for David. Lord, Thou didst test me and know me.
Thou knewest my sitting and my rising; Thou didst understand my reasonings from afar.
Thou didst trace my path and my measuring cord, and Thou didst foresee all my ways.
For there is no word on my tongue,
behold, Lord, Thou knewest all things, the last and the first; Thou didst form me and place Thy hand upon me.
Thy knowledge was made wondrous beyond me; it grew strong—I cannot reach it.
Where can I go from Thy Spirit, and where can I flee from Thy face?
If I ascend to heaven, Thou art there; if I descend into Hades, Thou art present.
if I take up my wings at dawn and settle at the sea’s farthest reaches,
indeed, even there Thy hand will guide me, and Thy right hand will hold me fast.
And I said, “Then darkness will trample me, and night is light in my delight.”
For darkness will not be dark from Thee, and night will be lit up like day; as its darkness, so also its light.
For Thou didst acquire my kidneys, Lord; Thou didst support me from my mother’s womb.
I will thank Thee, for I was made fearfully wonderful; wondrous are Thy works, and my soul knows very well.
My bone was not hidden from Thee, which Thou madest in secret, and my substance in earth’s lowest places.
Thine eyes saw my unworked substance, and in Thy book all will be written; they will be formed over days, and none among them.
Thy friends were greatly honored by me, God; their beginnings grew very strong.
I will count them, and they will multiply beyond the sand; I awoke, and I am still with Thee.
If Thou dost kill sinners, God— men of blood, turn away from me,
for Thou wilt speak into deliberation; they will take Thy cities into vanity.
Did I not hate those who hate Thee, Lord, and melt away over Thine enemies?
I hated them with complete hatred; they became enemies to me.
Test me, God, and know my heart; examine me and know my paths,
and see whether a way of lawlessness is in me, and guide me in an eternal way.
For the end. A psalm for David.
Rescue me, Lord, from an evil person; deliver me from an unjust man,
those who devised injustices in their heart and were arraying wars all day.
They sharpened their tongue like a serpent’s; asp venom is beneath their lips. Diapsalma.
Guard me, Lord, from a sinner’s hand; rescue me from unjust people, those who devised to trip my steps.
The proud hid a trap for me and stretched cords, traps for my feet; along the path they set a stumbling block for me. Diapsalma.
I said to the Lord, “Thou art my God.” Listen, Lord, to the voice of my petition.
Lord, Lord, power of my salvation, Thou didst overshadow my head on the day of war.
Do not hand me over to a sinner, Lord, through my desire; they schemed against me; do not abandon me, lest they rise high. Diapsalma.
The head of their encirclement— the trouble of their lips will cover them.
Coals will fall upon them; in fire Thou wilt cast them down; in miseries they will certainly not withstand.
A talkative man will not be set straight on the earth; evils will hunt an unjust man to destruction.
I knew that the Lord will act for the poor person’s judgment and the needy people’s cause.
Indeed, the righteous will thank Thy name, and the upright will dwell with Thy presence.
A psalm for David. Lord, I have cried unto Thee; hear me. Attend to the voice of my petition when I cry unto Thee.
Let my prayer be directed as incense before Thee, the lifting of my hands as an evening sacrifice.
Set a guard, Lord, for my mouth and a restraining door around my lips.
Do not turn my heart toward words of wickedness, to offer excuses for sins with people who practice lawlessness, and I will certainly not join with their chosen ones.
A righteous man will discipline me in mercy and correct me, but let a sinner’s oil not enrich my head, for still my prayer is amid their good pleasures.
Their judges were swallowed up beside a rock; they will hear my words, for they became sweet.
Like a clod of earth broken upon the earth, our bones were scattered beside Hades.
For my eyes are toward Thee, Lord, Lord; in Thee I hoped—do not take away my soul.
Guard me from the trap they assembled for me and from the stumbling blocks of those practicing lawlessness.
Sinners will fall into his casting net; I am alone until I pass by.
Of understanding, of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer.
With my voice I cried to the Lord; with my voice I pleaded with the Lord.
I will pour out my plea before Him; I will declare my affliction before Him.
When my spirit was failing within me, Thou knewest my paths. On this way where I was walking, they hid a trap for me.
I looked to the right and observed, for there was no one recognizing me. Escape perished from me, and there is no one seeking my soul.
I cried unto Thee, Lord; I said, Thou art my hope, my portion in the land of the living.
Attend to my plea, for I was brought very low. Rescue me from those pursuing me, for they grew stronger than I.
Bring my soul out of prison, that I may thank Thy name, Lord. The righteous will wait for me until Thou repayest me.
A psalm of David, when his son pursues him. Lord, hear my prayer; give ear to my plea in Thy truth. Answer me in Thy righteousness.
Do not enter into judgment with Thy servant, for no one living will be justified before Thee.
For the enemy pursued my soul, brought my life low to the ground, made me sit in dark places like those long dead.
My spirit grew despondent within me; within me my heart was troubled.
I remembered ancient days and meditated on all Thy works; I was pondering the works of Thy hands.
I spread out my hands unto Thee; my soul is like a waterless land for Thee. Diapsalma.
Quickly hear me, Lord; my spirit is spent. Do not turn Thy face away from me, or I shall become like those descending to the pit.
Make Thy mercy heard by me in the morning, for I hoped in Thee. Make known to me, Lord, the way I shall walk, for unto Thee I lifted my soul.
Take me out from my enemies, Lord, for I fled unto Thee for refuge.
Teach me to do Thy will, for Thou art my God. Thy good Spirit will lead me on level ground.
For Thy name’s sake, Lord, Thou wilt give me life; in Thy righteousness Thou wilt bring my soul out of distress.
In Thy mercy Thou wilt utterly destroy my enemies and destroy all who distress my soul, for I am Thy servant.
Of David, concerning Goliath. Blessed is the Lord, my God, who trains my hands for battle array, my fingers for war.
My mercy and my refuge, my Helper and my Rescuer, my Defender, in whom I hoped, who subjects my people beneath me.
Lord, what is man, that Thou becamest known to him, or a son of man, that Thou takest account of him?
A man was likened to futility; his days pass like a shadow.
Lord, bend Thy heavens and descend; touch the mountains, and they will smoke.
Flash lightning, and Thou wilt scatter them; send out Thine arrows, and Thou wilt throw them into confusion.
Send out Thy hand from on high; take me out and rescue me from many waters, from the hand of foreigners.
Whose mouth spoke futility, and whose right hand is a right hand of injustice.
God, I will sing a new song unto Thee; on a ten-stringed psaltery I will make music unto Thee.
To Him who gives salvation to kings, who redeems David His servant from an evil sword.
Rescue me and take me out from the hand of foreigners, whose mouth spoke futility and whose right hand is a right hand of injustice.
Whose sons are like young plants established in their youth, their daughters beautified, adorned all around like the likeness of a sanctuary.
Their storehouses full, pouring forth from this to that; their sheep bearing many young, multiplying in their outgoing places.
Their oxen fat; there is no collapse of a fence and no passage out, nor any cry in their squares.
They called happy the people who have these things; happy the people whose God is the Lord.
A praise of David. I will exalt Thee, my God, my King, and bless Thy name for the age and for the age of the age.
Every day I will bless Thee and praise Thy name for the age and for the age of the age.
Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised; His greatness has no limit.
Generation after generation will praise Thy works, and they will declare Thy power.
They will speak of the magnificence of the glory of Thy holiness, and they will recount Thy wonders.
They will speak of the power of Thy fearsome acts, and they will recount Thy greatness.
They will pour forth remembrance of the abundance of Thy kindness and rejoice in Thy righteousness.
Compassionate and merciful is the Lord, patient and abundant in mercy.
The Lord is kind to all, and His compassions are over all His works.
Let all Thy works give thanks unto Thee, Lord, and let Thy holy ones bless Thee.
They will speak of the glory of Thy kingdom and tell of Thy might,
to make known to the sons of men Thy might and the glory of the magnificence of Thy kingdom.
Thy kingdom is a kingdom of all ages, and Thy lordship endures through every generation.
Faithful is the Lord in His words, and holy in all His works.
The Lord supports all who are falling and raises up all who have been broken down.
The eyes of all hope in Thee, and Thou givest their food at the right time.
Thou openest Thy hand and fillest every living creature with good pleasure.
The Lord is righteous in all His ways and holy in all His works.
The Lord is near to all who call on Him, to all who call on Him in truth.
He will fulfill the will of those who fear Him; He will hear their plea and save them.
The Lord guards all who love Him, and all sinners He will utterly destroy.
My mouth will speak the Lord’s praise, and let all flesh bless His holy name for the age and for the age of the age.
Hallelujah. Of Haggai and Zechariah. Praise the Lord, my soul.
I will praise the Lord throughout my life; I will make music to my God as long as I exist.
Do not trust in rulers and in sons of men who have no salvation.
His spirit will go out, and he will return to his earth; on that day all their reasonings will perish.
Happy the one whose Helper is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the Lord his God,
who made heaven and earth, the sea and all that is in them, who keeps truth for ever,
who does justice for those wronged, who gives food to the hungry. The Lord releases those in fetters.
The Lord raises up those broken down; the Lord makes the blind wise; the Lord loves the righteous.
The Lord guards the newcomers; He will take up the orphan and widow, and He will obliterate the way of sinners.
The Lord will reign for ever, your God, Zion, through every generation.
Hallelujah. Of Haggai and Zechariah. Praise the Lord, for a psalm is good; may praise be pleasing to our God.
The Lord builds Jerusalem, and He will gather the dispersed of Israel.
He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their fractures.
He numbers multitudes of stars and calls them all by names.
Great is our Lord, and great is His strength; His understanding is beyond number.
The Lord takes up the meek, but brings sinners low to the ground.
Begin singing to the Lord with thanksgiving; make music to our God with a lyre,
who clothes heaven with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who makes grass sprout on the mountains and green growth for the service of humans,
who gives the cattle their food and to the young ravens who call upon Him.
He will not delight in the horse’s might, nor does He take pleasure in a man’s shins.
The Lord takes pleasure in those who fear Him and in those who hope in His mercy.
Hallelujah. Of Haggai and Zechariah. Commend the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion.
For He strengthened the bars of your gates; He blessed your children within you.
He makes your borders peaceful and fills you with the finest wheat.
He sends His oracle to the earth; His word will run swiftly,
of Him who gives snow like wool, who sprinkles mist like ashes,
who casts His ice like morsels; who will withstand His cold?
He will send His word and melt them; He will blow His wind, and waters will flow.
He declares His word to Jacob, His ordinances and judgments to Israel.
He did not do so for any nation, and He did not disclose His judgments to them.
Hallelujah. Of Haggai and Zechariah. Praise the Lord from the heavens; praise Him in the highest places.
Praise Him, all His angels; praise Him, all His powers.
Praise Him, sun and moon; praise Him, all the stars and the light.
Praise Him, heavens of heavens, and the water above the heavens.
Let them praise the Lord’s name, for He spoke, and they came to be; He commanded, and they were created.
He established them for the age and for the age of the age; He set a command, and it will not pass away.
Praise the Lord from the earth, dragons and all deeps,
fire, hail, snow, ice, storm wind—all fulfilling His word,
mountains and all hills, fruit-bearing trees and all cedars,
wild animals and all cattle, creeping things and winged birds,
kings of the earth and all peoples, rulers and all judges of the earth,
young men and young women, old people with younger people.
Let them praise the Lord’s name, for His name alone was exalted; His praise is over earth and heaven.
He will raise a horn of His people— a hymn for all His holy ones, for the children of Israel, a people drawing near to Him.
Hallelujah. Sing a new song to the Lord, His praise in the assembly of holy ones.
Let Israel rejoice in the One who made it, and let Zion’s children exult in their King.
Let them praise His name in a chorus; with tambourine and psaltery let them make music to Him.
For the Lord takes pleasure in His people, and He will exalt the meek in salvation.
Holy ones will boast in glory and rejoice upon their beds.
Exaltations of God in their throat, and two-edged swords in their hands,
to execute vengeance among the nations, reproofs among the peoples,
to bind their kings in fetters and their glorious ones in iron handcuffs,
to execute upon them a written judgment. This is glory for all His holy ones.
Hallelujah. Praise God among His holy ones; praise Him in the firmament of His power.
Praise Him for His mighty acts; praise Him according to the abundance of His greatness.
Praise Him with the sound of a trumpet; praise Him with psaltery and lyre.
Praise Him with tambourine and chorus; praise Him with strings and instrument.
Praise Him with well-sounding cymbals; praise Him with cymbals of a shout.
Let every breath praise the Lord. Hallelujah.

This psalm is personally written concerning David and is outside the number, when he fought Goliath in single combat. I was small among my brothers and younger in my father’s house; I was shepherding my father’s sheep.
My hands made an instrument; my fingers fitted a psaltery.
And who shall tell my Lord? He Himself is Lord; He Himself hears.
He Himself sent out His angel and took me from my father’s sheep and anointed me with the oil of His anointing.
My brothers were handsome and tall, but the Lord took no pleasure in them.
I went out to meet the foreigner, and he cursed me by his idols.
But I drew the sword he carried, cut off his head, and removed reproach from the sons of Israel.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Zion in captivity and restored gladness
final_complete_triples.rationale: Weeping beside Babylon’s rivers at the remembrance of Zion contrasts with the comfort, joyful mouths and gladness when Zion’s captivity is turned back. The comparison follows the named Zion and captivity setting without making the two poems one occasion.

source_unit.text: For David. By Babylon’s rivers, there we sat and wept when we remembered Zion.

target_units.text: A song of the ascents. When the Lord turned back Zion’s captivity, we became like those comforted.
Then our mouth was filled with joy and our tongue with exultation. Then they will say among the nations, “The Lord has done great things with them.”
The Lord has done great things with us; we became glad.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Silent music in mourning over Zion
final_complete_triples.rationale: Hanging the instruments amid Babylon’s captivity corresponds to chosen men ceasing from songs, joy ending and dancing turning to mourning because Mount Zion was destroyed. Lamentations does not mention willows or hung instruments; the specific link is the silence of music in the lament for Zion.

source_unit.text: Upon the willows in her midst we hung our instruments.

target_units.text: Elders ceased from the gate, chosen men ceased from their songs.
The joy of our heart ended; our dancing turned to mourning.
The crown fell from our head; woe indeed to us, for we sinned!
For this our heart became sorrowful; for this our eyes grew dim,
because Mount Zion was destroyed; foxes passed through her.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Captive songs and the joy of restored Zion
final_complete_triples.rationale: Captors demand songs of Zion here; the return of Zion’s captivity there fills the people’s mouths and tongues with joy. The speakers and circumstances differ, making the requested captive song and restored expression a concrete contrast.

source_unit.text: For there those who took us captive asked us for words of songs, and those who led us away for a hymn: “Sing us some of Zion’s songs.”

target_units.text: A song of the ascents. When the Lord turned back Zion’s captivity, we became like those comforted.
Then our mouth was filled with joy and our tongue with exultation. Then they will say among the nations, “The Lord has done great things with them.”

final_complete_triples.relationship: The Lord’s song abroad and restored Zion’s voice
final_complete_triples.rationale: The question about singing the Lord’s song on foreign land contrasts with the joyful mouth and tongue when Zion’s captivity is turned back. This does not supply a named location for Psalm 125 beyond Zion’s stated captivity.

source_unit.text: How can we sing the Lord’s song on foreign land?

target_units.text: A song of the ascents. When the Lord turned back Zion’s captivity, we became like those comforted.
Then our mouth was filled with joy and our tongue with exultation. Then they will say among the nations, “The Lord has done great things with them.”

final_complete_triples.relationship: Refusing to forget Jerusalem or Zion
final_complete_triples.rationale: The speaker binds himself not to forget Jerusalem; Isaiah answers Zion’s complaint of being forgotten with the Lord’s promise not to forget her and the image of her walls on His hands. Human self-imprecation and divine assurance remain distinct.

source_unit.text: If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand be forgotten.

target_units.text: But Zion said, “The Lord has abandoned me, and the Lord has forgotten me.”
“Will a woman forget her child, failing to have mercy on the offspring of her belly? Even if a woman forgets these, I will not forget you,” said the Lord.
“Behold, on My hands I painted your walls, and you are before Me continually.

final_complete_triples.relationship: A tongue stuck to the throat
final_complete_triples.rationale: The conditional curse for failing to remember Jerusalem uses the tongue clinging to the throat, while Psalm 21 describes that condition amid mortal distress. The shared bodily image does not identify the occasions.

source_unit.text: May my tongue cling to my throat if I do not remember you, if I do not set Jerusalem first at the beginning of my gladness.

target_units.text: My strength dried up like a potsherd; my tongue is stuck to my throat, and Thou broughtest me down into the dust of death.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Edom’s participation in Jerusalem’s calamity
final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm asks remembrance of Edom’s sons urging Jerusalem’s destruction. Obadiah’s address to Idumea describes opposition when strangers entered Jerusalem and forbids rejoicing, entering and attacking on the day of destruction. The specific quotations and actions are not collapsed into one speech.

source_unit.text: Remember, Lord, Edom’s sons on Jerusalem’s day, those saying, “Empty her, empty her, down to the foundation within her!”

target_units.text: From the day you stood opposed, on the day foreigners took his strength captive and strangers entered his gates and cast lots over Jerusalem, you too were like one of them.
Do not look on your brother’s day, on the day of strangers; do not rejoice over the sons of Judah on the day of their destruction; do not speak boastfully on the day of affliction.

Do not enter the gates of peoples on the day of their suffering. You, too, must not look on their assembly on the day of their destruction, and do not join in attacking their strength on the day of their destruction.
Do not stand at their escape routes to destroy those of them who are being saved, and do not shut in those fleeing from them on the day of affliction.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Babylon repaid according to what she did
final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm calls happy the one repaying Babylon the repayment she gave; Jeremiah commands that Babylon be repaid according to her works and treated as she treated others. Both explicitly name Babylon and reciprocal recompense.

source_unit.text: Daughter Babylon, miserable one, happy is the one who will repay you the repayment you gave us.

target_units.text: A sound of those fleeing and being rescued from Babylon’s land, announcing in Zion vengeance from the Lord our God!

Give orders against Babylon to many, to everyone drawing a bow. Encamp against her all around; let none of her people escape. Repay her according to her works; do to her all she did, for she resisted the Lord, Israel’s holy God.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Children dashed in judgment against Babylon
final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm’s violent blessing concerning Babylon’s infants corresponds to Isaiah’s Babylon oracle describing their children dashed before them. Isaiah does not specify the psalm’s rock, and the comparison reports the texts rather than extending their command to another setting.

source_unit.text: Happy is the one who will seize your infants and dash them against the rock.

target_units.text: They will dash their children before them, plunder their houses and take possession of their wives.
Behold, I am rousing the Medes against you, who do not value silver or have need of gold.
They will shatter young men’s arrows and certainly not pity your children; their eyes will not spare the children.
Babylon, which is called glorious by the king of the Chaldeans, will be as when God overturned Sodom and Gomorrah.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Wholehearted thanksgiving and music to God
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both first-person prayers promise thanksgiving with the whole heart and music or sung praise to God. Psalm 137 adds heard speech and angels; Psalm 9 adds the recounting of wonders.

source_unit.text: For David. I will thank Thee, Lord, with all my heart, for Thou heardest the words of my mouth, and before angels I will make music unto Thee.

target_units.text: I will give thanks unto Thee, Lord, with my whole heart; I will recount all Thy wonders.
I will rejoice and exult in Thee; I will sing praise to Thy name, Most High.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Bowing toward the holy temple
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both speakers bow toward God’s holy temple in a context naming His mercy. Psalm 137 adds thanksgiving for mercy and truth; Psalm 5 describes entering the house and bowing in fear.

source_unit.text: I will bow toward Thy holy temple and thank Thy name for Thy mercy and Thy truth, for Thou hast magnified Thine utterance above every name.

target_units.text: But I, through the multitude of Thy mercy, will enter Thy house; I will bow toward Thy holy temple in fear of Thee.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Hear quickly on the day of calling
final_complete_triples.rationale: The petition on whatever day the speaker calls, asking to be heard quickly, closely repeats Psalm 101’s concluding plea. Psalm 137’s strengthening of the soul is an additional element.

source_unit.text: On whatever day I call Thee, hear me quickly; Thou wilt greatly attend to me with strength in my soul.

target_units.text: Do not turn Thy face away from me. On whatever day I am afflicted, incline Thine ear to me; on whatever day I call upon Thee, hear me quickly.

final_complete_triples.relationship: All earth’s kings respond to the Lord
final_complete_triples.rationale: The summons for all earth’s kings to thank the Lord after hearing His words corresponds to all the kings of the earth fearing His glory in Psalm 101. Thanksgiving and fear are distinguished.

source_unit.text: Let all earth’s kings thank Thee, Lord, for they heard all the words of Thy mouth.

target_units.text: Nations will fear the Lord’s name, and all the kings of the earth Thy glory,

final_complete_triples.relationship: Singing in view of the Lord’s great glory
final_complete_triples.rationale: Singing in the Lord’s ways because His glory is great corresponds to announcing His glory and declaring the Lord great and greatly to be praised. The passages unite the stated glory, greatness and sung praise without treating ways and nations as the same object.

source_unit.text: And let them sing in the Lord’s ways, for great is the Lord’s glory.

target_units.text: Announce His glory among the nations, His wonders among all the peoples.
For great is the Lord and greatly to be praised; He is fearsome above all gods.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The high Lord attends to the lowly
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord’s height and regard for the lowly parallel His high dwelling and looking upon lowly things, followed by raising the poor. Psalm 137’s knowledge of the lofty from afar is not imported into the target.

source_unit.text: For the Lord is high and watches the lowly, and the lofty He knows from afar.

target_units.text: Who is like the Lord our God, who dwells in high places,
and looks upon lowly things in heaven and on earth?
He raises the poor from the ground and lifts the needy from the dung heap,

final_complete_triples.relationship: Preservation amid affliction and hostile power
final_complete_triples.rationale: The speaker’s life is preserved amid affliction and enemies’ anger; Psalm 17 describes enemies overtaking him on the day of affliction and the Lord becoming his support and rescuer. The right-hand wording belongs to Psalm 137, not the selected target.

source_unit.text: If I walk amid affliction, Thou wilt keep me alive; against my enemies’ anger Thou didst stretch out Thy hand, and Thy right hand saved me.

target_units.text: He will rescue me from my powerful enemies and from those who hate me, for they grew stronger than I.
They overtook me in the day of my affliction, and the Lord became my support,
and He brought me out into a spacious place. He will rescue me because He desired me. He will rescue me from my powerful enemies and from those who hate me.

final_complete_triples.relationship: A plea concerning the work of God’s hands
final_complete_triples.rationale: The plea not to neglect the works of God’s hands can be compared with Job’s appeal that those hands made him, followed by his complaint of being struck and remembrance of life and mercy. The speakers’ differing expectations are preserved.

source_unit.text: The Lord will repay on my behalf. Lord, Thy mercy is for ever; do not neglect the works of Thy hands.

target_units.text: Thy hands molded me and made me; afterward Thou didst change and strike me.
Remember that Thou didst mold me as clay, and Thou art turning me back again into earth.
Didst Thou not milk me out like milk and curdle me just like cheese?
Thou didst clothe me with skin and flesh and thread me together with bones and sinews.
Thou didst place life and mercy beside me, and Thy care guarded my spirit.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Divine testing of the speaker
final_complete_triples.rationale: Psalm 138 begins by affirming that the Lord tested and knew the speaker; Psalm 25 asks the Lord to test and try the speaker’s kidneys and heart. An accomplished testing and a requested testing are distinguished.

source_unit.text: For the end. A psalm for David. Lord, Thou didst test me and know me.

target_units.text: Test me, Lord, and try me; try my kidneys and my heart by fire.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The Lord knows human reasonings
final_complete_triples.rationale: Knowledge of the speaker’s reasonings from afar corresponds to the Lord knowing human reasonings in Psalm 93. The latter calls them futile, a judgment not stated in this source unit.

source_unit.text: Thou knewest my sitting and my rising; Thou didst understand my reasonings from afar.

target_units.text: The Lord knows human reasonings, that they are futile.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Human ways and tracks before God
final_complete_triples.rationale: God traced the speaker’s path and foresaw all his ways; Proverbs places a man’s ways before God’s eyes and says He watches all his tracks. The psalm’s measuring cord is not supplied to Proverbs.

source_unit.text: Thou didst trace my path and my measuring cord, and Thou didst foresee all my ways.

target_units.text: For a man’s ways are before God’s eyes, and He watches all his tracks.

final_complete_triples.relationship: God’s forming hands upon the person
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord’s forming the speaker and placing His hand upon him corresponds to Job’s assertion that God’s hands molded and made him. Job’s subsequent complaint that God changed and struck him gives the comparison a different emotional setting.

source_unit.text: behold, Lord, Thou knewest all things, the last and the first; Thou didst form me and place Thy hand upon me.

target_units.text: Thy hands molded me and made me; afterward Thou didst change and strike me.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Wonderful divine knowledge beyond the speaker
final_complete_triples.rationale: The speaker cannot reach God’s wondrous knowledge; Job acknowledges great and wonderful things he did not understand. Neither statement is expanded into knowledge of an unstated event.

source_unit.text: Thy knowledge was made wondrous beyond me; it grew strong—I cannot reach it.

target_units.text: For who is the one hiding counsel from Thee, who withholds words and thinks he hides them from Thee? Who will announce to me what I did not know, great and wonderful things I did not understand?

final_complete_triples.relationship: No hiding from God’s presence
final_complete_triples.rationale: The questions about fleeing God’s Spirit and face correspond to the Lord’s question whether someone hiding can escape His sight and His filling heaven and earth. The different terms Spirit, face and sight remain intact.

source_unit.text: Where can I go from Thy Spirit, and where can I flee from Thy face?

target_units.text: I am a God drawing near, says the Lord, and not a God far away.
If a person hides in hidden places, will I not see him? Do I not fill the heaven and the earth? says the Lord.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Heaven and Hades cannot remove divine reach
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both passages explicitly pair ascent to heaven and descent into Hades with God’s presence or reach. The psalm affirms presence; Amos announces inescapable judgment.

source_unit.text: If I ascend to heaven, Thou art there; if I descend into Hades, Thou art present.

target_units.text: If they burrow into Hades, My hand will pull them up from there; if they climb to heaven, I will bring them down from there.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Departure across the sea cannot escape the Lord
final_complete_triples.rationale: Within the psalm’s question about fleeing God’s face, settling at the sea’s farthest reaches can be compared with Jonah’s attempt to sail to Tarshish from the Lord’s presence and the Lord’s action upon the sea. No geographical identity for the psalm’s destination is asserted.

source_unit.text: if I take up my wings at dawn and settle at the sea’s farthest reaches,

target_units.text: But Jonah rose to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the Lord. He went down to Joppa, found a ship traveling to Tarshish, paid its fare and boarded it, to sail with them to Tarshish from the presence of the Lord.
The Lord stirred up a wind upon the sea, and there was a great surge on the sea; the ship was in danger of being shattered.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Divine handholding and guidance
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both passages combine divine holding and guidance. Psalm 138 says God’s right hand holds the speaker; Psalm 72 says God grasped the speaker’s right hand and guided him in counsel.

source_unit.text: indeed, even there Thy hand will guide me, and Thy right hand will hold me fast.

target_units.text: And I am continually with Thee; Thou didst grasp my right hand.
In Thy counsel Thou didst guide me, and with glory Thou didst receive me.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Darkness does not exclude divine knowledge
final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm says darkness is not dark from God and night is lit like day; Daniel says He reveals dark things and knows what is in darkness and light. The comparison preserves Daniel’s actual knowledge wording rather than adding a different concluding light clause.

source_unit.text: For darkness will not be dark from Thee, and night will be lit up like day; as its darkness, so also its light.

target_units.text: reveals deep and dark things, knows what is in darkness and what is in light, and with Him is a dwelling.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Divine support from the mother’s womb
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both speakers explicitly describe being supported from the womb. Psalm 138 adds the acquiring of kidneys; Psalm 70 names shelter from the mother’s belly.

source_unit.text: For Thou didst acquire my kidneys, Lord; Thou didst support me from my mother’s womb.

target_units.text: Upon Thee I was supported from the womb; from my mother’s belly Thou art the One who shelters me. My hymn is continually in Thee.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The person wonderfully fashioned by God
final_complete_triples.rationale: Thanksgiving for the speaker’s wonderful making corresponds to Job’s description of God molding him and clothing or threading his body together. The relation is bodily divine workmanship; Job’s distressed protest is not turned into thanksgiving.

source_unit.text: I will thank Thee, for I was made fearfully wonderful; wondrous are Thy works, and my soul knows very well.

target_units.text: Thy hands molded me and made me; afterward Thou didst change and strike me.
Remember that Thou didst mold me as clay, and Thou art turning me back again into earth.
Didst Thou not milk me out like milk and curdle me just like cheese?
Thou didst clothe me with skin and flesh and thread me together with bones and sinews.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Hidden bodily formation and God’s works
final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm says the speaker’s bone and secretly made substance were not hidden from God; Ecclesiastes uses bones in a pregnant woman’s womb to illustrate human ignorance of God’s works. Divine knowledge and human ignorance are contrasted without equating earth’s lowest places with the womb.

source_unit.text: My bone was not hidden from Thee, which Thou madest in secret, and my substance in earth’s lowest places.

target_units.text: among which no one knows the way of the spirit. As with bones in the womb of the pregnant woman, so you will not know God’s works, all that He will make.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Separation from sinners and men of blood
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source commands men of blood to turn away while addressing God concerning sinners; Psalm 25 asks not to have the speaker’s life destroyed together with ungodly people and men of bloodshed. Desired separation is shared, while the source’s conditional opening is preserved.

source_unit.text: If Thou dost kill sinners, God— men of blood, turn away from me,

target_units.text: Do not destroy my soul together with the ungodly, or my life with men of bloodshed,

final_complete_triples.relationship: The speaker’s aversion to God’s opponents
final_complete_triples.rationale: The speaker’s hatred of those hating the Lord corresponds to hatred of an assembly of evildoers and refusal to sit with the ungodly. This is a comparison of stated opposition, not an equation of every named group or person.

source_unit.text: Did I not hate those who hate Thee, Lord, and melt away over Thine enemies?

target_units.text: I hated an assembly of evildoers, and I will certainly not sit with the ungodly.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Declared hatred of God’s opponents or lawbreakers
final_complete_triples.rationale: Complete hatred of the Lord’s enemies can be compared with the declared hatred of lawbreakers alongside love of His law. The target identifies lawbreakers; it does not repeat the source’s complete-hatred wording.

source_unit.text: I hated them with complete hatred; they became enemies to me.

target_units.text: Fifteen: Samch. I hated lawbreakers, and I loved Thy law.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Testing the inward person
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both petitions ask God to test the speaker and examine the heart. Psalm 138 adds knowledge of paths, while Psalm 25 names kidneys and trying by fire.

source_unit.text: Test me, God, and know my heart; examine me and know my paths,

target_units.text: Test me, Lord, and try me; try my kidneys and my heart by fire.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Guidance away from a wrong way
final_complete_triples.rationale: The request to detect a way of lawlessness and guide in an eternal way corresponds to the request for divine guidance in righteousness and a straight way before the speaker. Eternal duration is stated only in Psalm 138.

source_unit.text: and see whether a way of lawlessness is in me, and guide me in an eternal way.

target_units.text: Lord, guide me in Thy righteousness because of my enemies; direct Thy way straight before me.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Rescue from an unjust man
final_complete_triples.rationale: The plea to be delivered from an unjust man closely corresponds to Psalm 17’s assurance that the Lord will rescue the speaker from an unjust man. The source also names an evil person.

source_unit.text: Rescue me, Lord, from an evil person; deliver me from an unjust man,

target_units.text: my rescuer from my wrathful enemies. Thou wilt raise me above those who rise against me; Thou wilt rescue me from an unjust man.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Continual hostile thought against the speaker
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source’s people devise injustices in their heart and array wars all day; Psalm 55 describes all-day hostility toward the speaker’s words and thoughts against him for evil. Literal war is not added to the target.

source_unit.text: those who devised injustices in their heart and were arraying wars all day.

target_units.text: All day they detested my words; all their thoughts against me are for evil.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Asp venom beneath the lips
final_complete_triples.rationale: Romans’ written-text sequence includes the poison of asps under their lips, corresponding closely to this psalm’s asp venom beneath their lips. The psalm’s sharpened serpent-like tongue differs from the target’s deceitful tongues.

source_unit.text: They sharpened their tongue like a serpent’s; asp venom is beneath their lips. Diapsalma.

target_units.text: Their throat is an opened tomb; with their tongues they practiced deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips;

final_complete_triples.relationship: Hostile attention to the speaker’s feet
final_complete_triples.rationale: The plea against unjust people who devise to trip the speaker’s steps corresponds to concealed adversaries watching his heel and waiting for his soul. The relation rests on predatory pursuit expressed through steps or heel.

source_unit.text: Guard me, Lord, from a sinner’s hand; rescue me from unjust people, those who devised to trip my steps.

target_units.text: They will sojourn and conceal themselves; they will watch my heel, just as they waited for my soul.

final_complete_triples.relationship: A trap concealed on the speaker’s path
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both passages explicitly place an enemy-hidden trap on the path where the speaker walks. Psalm 139 adds cords, feet and a stumbling block.

source_unit.text: The proud hid a trap for me and stretched cords, traps for my feet; along the path they set a stumbling block for me. Diapsalma.

target_units.text: When my spirit was failing within me, Thou knewest my paths. On this way where I was walking, they hid a trap for me.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The confession Thou art my God
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both speakers say to the Lord, Thou art my God, while trusting Him amid surrounding adversaries. Psalm 139 adds a petition to listen; Psalm 30 states the speaker’s hope.

source_unit.text: I said to the Lord, “Thou art my God.” Listen, Lord, to the voice of my petition.

target_units.text: But I hoped in Thee, Lord; I said, “Thou art my God.”

final_complete_triples.relationship: Do not hand the speaker over to wrongdoers
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both petitions ask not to be handed over to hostile wrongdoers. Psalm 139’s through-my-desire clause remains uninterpreted; Psalm 26 specifies unjust witnesses and afflicters.

source_unit.text: Do not hand me over to a sinner, Lord, through my desire; they schemed against me; do not abandon me, lest they rise high. Diapsalma.

target_units.text: Do not hand me over to the souls of those who afflict me, for unjust witnesses rose against me, and injustice lied to itself.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Trouble returning upon the hostile head
final_complete_triples.rationale: The trouble of the encirclers’ lips covering them corresponds to trouble returning on an evildoer’s head and injustice descending upon his crown. The source’s compressed head-of-encirclement wording is preserved rather than replaced with a named leader.

source_unit.text: The head of their encirclement— the trouble of their lips will cover them.

target_units.text: His trouble will return upon his head, and his injustice will descend upon his crown.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Fire among the punishments of sinners
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source describes coals falling and being cast into fire; Psalm 10 names fire and sulfur in the sinners’ cup portion after raining traps. The target is not said to rain coals or fire.

source_unit.text: Coals will fall upon them; in fire Thou wilt cast them down; in miseries they will certainly not withstand.

target_units.text: He will rain traps upon sinners; fire, sulfur, and a storm wind are the portion of their cup.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Evil or lawless acts hunt a person
final_complete_triples.rationale: Evils hunting the unjust man to destruction correspond to lawless acts hunting a man in Proverbs. The target adds bondage by his own sins; the source also judges the talkative man.

source_unit.text: A talkative man will not be set straight on the earth; evils will hunt an unjust man to destruction.

target_units.text: Lawless acts hunt a man, and each is bound tight by the cords of his own sins.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Judgment for poor and needy people
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord’s action for the poor person’s judgment and needy people’s cause corresponds to the royal prayer for judgment of the poor and rescue of the children of the needy. The Lord and the king receiving His judgment are not treated as identical agents.

source_unit.text: I knew that the Lord will act for the poor person’s judgment and the needy people’s cause.

target_units.text: to judge Thy people in righteousness, and Thy poor in justice.
Let the mountains take up peace for Thy people, and the hills in righteousness.
He will judge the poor of the people, and save the children of the needy, and humble the false accuser,

final_complete_triples.relationship: Righteousness in God’s presence
final_complete_triples.rationale: The upright dwelling with God’s presence corresponds to the first-person hope of appearing before His face in righteousness. The thanksgiving clause and satisfaction at appearing glory are distinct additions.

source_unit.text: Indeed, the righteous will thank Thy name, and the upright will dwell with Thy presence.

target_units.text: But I, in righteousness, will appear before Thy face; I will be satisfied when Thy glory appears.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Crying and pleading to the Lord with the voice
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source’s cry and plea for attention to the voice of petition closely correspond to the twice-stated voice crying and pleading to the Lord in Psalm 141.

source_unit.text: A psalm for David. Lord, I have cried unto Thee; hear me. Attend to the voice of my petition when I cry unto Thee.

target_units.text: With my voice I cried to the Lord; with my voice I pleaded with the Lord.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Prayer compared with incense and prayer at the incense hour
final_complete_triples.rationale: The comparison of prayer with incense can be read alongside the people praying at the hour when the priest burns incense. The psalm is a prayer-image, whereas Luke narrates simultaneous temple actions.

source_unit.text: Let my prayer be directed as incense before Thee, the lifting of my hands as an evening sacrifice.

target_units.text: according to the priesthood’s custom, he was chosen by lot to enter the Lord’s sanctuary and burn incense.
The whole multitude of the people was praying outside at the hour of incense.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Raised hands compared with the evening sacrifice
final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm compares the lifting of hands to an evening sacrifice; Exodus prescribes the second daily lamb in the evening as a continual offering. The hands are a comparison, not a claim that the speaker performs the prescribed lamb offering.

source_unit.text: Let my prayer be directed as incense before Thee, the lifting of my hands as an evening sacrifice.

target_units.text: Offer one lamb in the morning and the second in the evening.
With one lamb offer a tenth measure of fine flour mixed with a quarter hin of beaten oil, and a quarter hin of wine as a libation.
Offer the second lamb in the evening, with the same sacrifice and libation as in the morning, as a fragrant aroma, an offering to the Lord,
as a continual sacrifice throughout your generations, at the doors of the Tent of Testimony before the Lord, where I will be made known to you, to speak to you.

final_complete_triples.relationship: A guard over the mouth against sinful speech
final_complete_triples.rationale: The request for a guard over the mouth and restraining door around lips corresponds to the speaker placing a guard upon his mouth so as not to sin with his tongue. Petition and stated self-restraint differ.

source_unit.text: Set a guard, Lord, for my mouth and a restraining door around my lips.

target_units.text: I said, “I will guard my ways so as not to sin with my tongue.” I placed a guard upon my mouth when the sinner stood against me.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Guarding heart and speech from wickedness
final_complete_triples.rationale: The petition not to turn the heart toward wicked words and sinful excuses corresponds to guarding the heart and removing crooked mouth and unjust lips. Proverbs’ instructions are not represented as the same excuse-making scene.

source_unit.text: Do not turn my heart toward words of wickedness, to offer excuses for sins with people who practice lawlessness, and I will certainly not join with their chosen ones.

target_units.text: With every guard keep your heart, for from these come life’s outlets.
Remove a crooked mouth from yourself and thrust unjust lips far away from you.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Beneficial correction contrasted with an enemy’s pleasant treatment
final_complete_triples.rationale: The righteous person’s merciful discipline and correction, contrasted with a sinner’s oil, can be compared with open rebuke and trustworthy wounds of a friend against an enemy’s willing kisses. Oil and kisses are distinct images, and the psalm’s final prayer clause is not resolved by the comparison.

source_unit.text: A righteous man will discipline me in mercy and correct me, but let a sinner’s oil not enrich my head, for still my prayer is amid their good pleasures.

target_units.text: Open rebukes are better than concealed friendship.
A friend’s wounds are more trustworthy than an enemy’s willing kisses.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Scattered bones in the speaker’s distress
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source’s scattered bones beside Hades correspond to the scattered bones in Psalm 21’s bodily distress. The clod-of-earth image and location beside Hades are not added to the target.

source_unit.text: Like a clod of earth broken upon the earth, our bones were scattered beside Hades.

target_units.text: I was poured out like water, and all my bones were scattered. My heart became like wax melting in the midst of my belly.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Eyes directed toward the Lord in dependence
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source directs its eyes toward the Lord and says it hoped in Him; Psalm 122 lifts eyes to Him and compares that attention with servants looking to their masters’ hands, continuing until divine compassion.

source_unit.text: For my eyes are toward Thee, Lord, Lord; in Thee I hoped—do not take away my soul.

target_units.text: A song of the ascents. To Thee I lifted my eyes, Thou who dwellest in heaven.
Behold, as slaves’ eyes turn to their masters’ hands, as a slave woman’s eyes turn to her mistress’s hands, so our eyes turn to the Lord our God, until He has compassion on us.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Protection from sinners’ traps
final_complete_triples.rationale: The plea to be guarded from the assembled trap and lawless stumbling blocks corresponds to sinners setting a trap while the speaker remains with God’s commandments. The target states fidelity rather than explicitly repeating the source’s protection request.

source_unit.text: Guard me from the trap they assembled for me and from the stumbling blocks of those practicing lawlessness.

target_units.text: Sinners set a trap for me, and I did not wander from Thy commandments.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Wrongdoers caught in a destructive device
final_complete_triples.rationale: Sinners falling into his casting net correspond to the evildoer falling into the pit he dug. The source’s his is left unassigned, and a net is not called a pit.

source_unit.text: Sinners will fall into his casting net; I am alone until I pass by.

target_units.text: Behold, he was in labor with injustice; he conceived trouble and gave birth to lawlessness.
He dug a pit and hollowed it out, and he will fall into the hole he made.

final_complete_triples.relationship: David and a cave in psalm headings
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both headings place David in a cave. Psalm 56 explicitly names escape from Saul; Psalm 141 does not name the pursuer or specify which cave. The shared heading information does not prove one historical occasion.

source_unit.text: Of understanding, of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer.

target_units.text: For the end. Do not destroy. Of David, for an inscription on a pillar, when he escaped from Saul’s presence into the cave.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Repeated voice crying to the Lord
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both lines repeat with my voice in describing the cry to the Lord. Psalm 141’s second action is pleading; Psalm 76 continues with God attending to the speaker.

source_unit.text: With my voice I cried to the Lord; with my voice I pleaded with the Lord.

target_units.text: With my voice I cried to the Lord, with my voice to God, and He attended to me.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Pouring out the inward plea before God
final_complete_triples.rationale: The speaker will pour out his plea before God and declare affliction; Psalm 61 tells the assembly to pour out their hearts before Him. The individual plea and the communal heart image are distinguished.

source_unit.text: I will pour out my plea before Him; I will declare my affliction before Him.

target_units.text: Hope in Him, all the assembly of the people; pour out your hearts before Him. God is our helper. Diapsalma.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The failing or despondent spirit within
final_complete_triples.rationale: The spirit failing within the speaker closely corresponds to the spirit growing despondent within and the troubled heart in Psalm 142. The source continues with God’s knowledge and a trap, details not supplied to the target.

source_unit.text: When my spirit was failing within me, Thou knewest my paths. On this way where I was walking, they hid a trap for me.

target_units.text: My spirit grew despondent within me; within me my heart was troubled.

final_complete_triples.relationship: No human companion or comforter found
final_complete_triples.rationale: The speaker looks and finds no one recognizing or seeking him; Psalm 68 waits for someone to grieve with him and finds no comforter. Seeking the speaker’s soul is retained as written, not turned into an enemy pursuing him.

source_unit.text: I looked to the right and observed, for there was no one recognizing me. Escape perished from me, and there is no one seeking my soul.

target_units.text: My soul expected reproach and misery; I waited for someone to grieve with me, but there was none, for comforters, but found none.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The Lord as the speaker’s portion
final_complete_triples.rationale: Calling the Lord the speaker’s portion in the land of the living corresponds to the Lord as the portion of inheritance and cup. Neither passage identifies the portion as a literal land allotment.

source_unit.text: I cried unto Thee, Lord; I said, Thou art my hope, my portion in the land of the living.

target_units.text: The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and my cup; Thou art the One who restores my inheritance to me.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Rescue from pursuers stronger than the speaker
final_complete_triples.rationale: The plea for rescue because pursuers grew stronger than the speaker closely corresponds to Psalm 17’s rescue from powerful enemies who grew stronger than him.

source_unit.text: Attend to my plea, for I was brought very low. Rescue me from those pursuing me, for they grew stronger than I.

target_units.text: He will rescue me from my powerful enemies and from those who hate me, for they grew stronger than I.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Release from confinement followed by thanksgiving
final_complete_triples.rationale: The request to bring the soul out of prison in order to thank God corresponds to rescue, broken bonds and a summons to acknowledge His mercies. The psalm’s soul-prison language is not assigned the target’s particular captivity or cause.

source_unit.text: Bring my soul out of prison, that I may thank Thy name, Lord. The righteous will wait for me until Thou repayest me.

target_units.text: They cried to the Lord when they were afflicted, and He saved them from their distresses,
and brought them out of darkness and death’s shadow and broke their bonds apart.
Let them acknowledge to the Lord His mercies and His wonders to the sons of men,
for He shattered bronze gates and broke iron bars.

final_complete_triples.relationship: David endangered by his son
final_complete_triples.rationale: The heading identifies David pursued by his son; the narrative describes David fleeing the danger from Absalom, identified earlier as his son. It supplies a concrete comparable father-son crisis without proving the poem’s composition date or equating every detail.

source_unit.text: A psalm of David, when his son pursues him. Lord, hear my prayer; give ear to my plea in Thy truth. Answer me in Thy righteousness.

target_units.text: A messenger came to David, saying, “The hearts of the men of Israel have gone after Absalom.”

David said to all his servants with him in Jerusalem, “Rise, let us flee, for we have no deliverance from Absalom. Hurry to leave, lest he hurry and overtake us, thrust calamity upon us, and strike the city with the sword’s edge.”

final_complete_triples.relationship: No living person justified before God
final_complete_triples.rationale: The plea not to enter judgment because no living person will be justified before God corresponds to Romans’ statement that no flesh will be justified before Him by works of law. The law qualification belongs to Romans, not this psalm’s wording.

source_unit.text: Do not enter into judgment with Thy servant, for no one living will be justified before Thee.

target_units.text: because by works of law no flesh will be justified before Him, for through law comes knowledge of sin.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Human righteousness before God’s judgment
final_complete_triples.rationale: Job asks how a mortal can be righteous before the Lord and considers entering judgment with Him; the psalm asks God not to enter judgment with His servant because no living person will be justified before Him. Job’s actual denied-hearing wording is preserved.

source_unit.text: Do not enter into judgment with Thy servant, for no one living will be justified before Thee.

target_units.text: “Truly I know that it is so; for how can a mortal be righteous before the Lord?
For if he wishes to enter judgment with Him, He certainly will not listen to him, lest he answer back to one of His words out of a thousand.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Dwelling in darkness like the long dead
final_complete_triples.rationale: The enemy’s making the speaker sit in dark places like those long dead closely corresponds to Lamentations’ dwelling in dark places like the dead of ages. The surrounding agents differ and are not equated.

source_unit.text: For the enemy pursued my soul, brought my life low to the ground, made me sit in dark places like those long dead.

target_units.text: He made me dwell in dark places like the dead of ages.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The spirit loses heart amid distress
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source’s despondent spirit and troubled heart correspond to Psalm 76’s spirit losing heart after extended speech. Remembering God and gladness in the target are not omitted to claim identical emotional sequences.

source_unit.text: My spirit grew despondent within me; within me my heart was troubled.

target_units.text: I remembered God and was glad; I spoke at length, and my spirit lost heart. Diapsalma.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Remembering and meditating on God’s works
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both speakers remember the Lord’s works and meditate on all His works. Psalm 142 also names ancient days, while Psalm 76 names wonders from the beginning.

source_unit.text: I remembered ancient days and meditated on all Thy works; I was pondering the works of Thy hands.

target_units.text: I remembered the Lord’s works, for I will remember Thy wonders from the beginning,
and meditate on all Thy works, and speak at length about Thy practices.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The soul’s longing expressed through waterless land
final_complete_triples.rationale: The soul like a waterless land for God corresponds to the soul thirsting for Him and flesh longing in a waterless wilderness. The source compares the soul to land; the target situates longing in that landscape.

source_unit.text: I spread out my hands unto Thee; my soul is like a waterless land for Thee. Diapsalma.

target_units.text: God, my God, toward Thee I rise at dawn; my soul thirsted for Thee. How greatly my flesh longs for Thee in a desert, trackless and waterless land!

final_complete_triples.relationship: Hear lest the speaker resemble those entering the pit
final_complete_triples.rationale: Psalm 142 asks quick hearing and an unaverted face lest the speaker become like those descending to the pit; Psalm 27 asks that God not remain silent lest he become like those descending into a pit.

source_unit.text: Quickly hear me, Lord; my spirit is spent. Do not turn Thy face away from me, or I shall become like those descending to the pit.

target_units.text: Of David. To Thee, Lord, I cried; my God, do not keep silence toward me, lest Thou keep silence toward me and I become like those descending into a pit.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The lifted soul asks to know God’s way
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both prayers combine lifting the soul to God, trusting or hoping in Him, and asking to know the way to walk. Psalm 142’s morning mercy is an additional specification.

source_unit.text: Make Thy mercy heard by me in the morning, for I hoped in Thee. Make known to me, Lord, the way I shall walk, for unto Thee I lifted my soul.

target_units.text: A psalm of David. To Thee, Lord, I lifted my soul, my God.
In Thee I have trusted; may I not be put to shame, and let my enemies not laugh at me.
For indeed, all who wait for Thee will certainly not be put to shame; let all who act lawlessly without cause be ashamed.
Make Thy ways known to me, Lord, and teach me Thy paths.
Guide me into Thy truth and teach me, for Thou art God my Savior, and I waited for Thee the whole day.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Refuge in God and rescue from enemies
final_complete_triples.rationale: The plea for rescue from enemies because the speaker fled to God for refuge corresponds to the confession of God as refuge and rescuer followed by salvation from enemies. No particular flight is inferred.

source_unit.text: Take me out from my enemies, Lord, for I fled unto Thee for refuge.

target_units.text: The Lord is my firm foundation, my refuge, and my rescuer; my God is my helper, and I will hope in Him; my protector, the horn of my salvation, my supporter.
Praising, I will call upon the Lord, and I will be saved from my enemies.

final_complete_triples.relationship: God’s good Spirit teaches and guides
final_complete_triples.rationale: The request to be taught God’s will and the affirmation that His good Spirit will lead the speaker correspond to the account of wilderness guidance and the gift of His good Spirit for understanding. Level ground is stated only in the psalm.

source_unit.text: Teach me to do Thy will, for Thou art my God. Thy good Spirit will lead me on level ground.

target_units.text: “Thou, in Thine abundant compassion, didst not abandon them in the wilderness. Thou didst not turn the pillar of cloud away from them by day, to guide them on the way, or the pillar of fire by night, to light for them the way they should travel.
“Thou gavest Thy good Spirit to give them understanding. Thou didst not withhold Thy manna from their mouths, and Thou gavest them water for their thirst.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Name and righteousness in divine guidance or restoration
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source expects life for God’s name’s sake and deliverance in His righteousness; Psalm 22 describes restoration of the soul and guidance in paths of righteousness for His name’s sake. The particular restoration and direction images differ.

source_unit.text: For Thy name’s sake, Lord, Thou wilt give me life; in Thy righteousness Thou wilt bring my soul out of distress.

target_units.text: He turned my soul back; He guided me upon paths of righteousness for His name’s sake.

final_complete_triples.relationship: God’s support and destruction of the speaker’s enemies
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source expects the destruction of enemies and afflicters in God’s mercy; Psalm 53 joins divine support of the soul with turning evils on enemies and a petition to destroy them in truth. Mercy and truth remain the respective grounds stated.

source_unit.text: In Thy mercy Thou wilt utterly destroy my enemies and destroy all who distress my soul, for I am Thy servant.

target_units.text: For behold, God helps me, and the Lord is the supporter of my soul.
He will turn the evils back upon my enemies; in Thy truth, utterly destroy them.

final_complete_triples.relationship: God trains hands for war
final_complete_triples.rationale: The blessing of God who trains the speaker’s hands for battle closely repeats the training of hands for war in Psalm 17. The source adds fingers and its Goliath heading; the target adds the bronze bow.

source_unit.text: Of David, concerning Goliath. Blessed is the Lord, my God, who trains my hands for battle array, my fingers for war.

target_units.text: training my hands for war; and Thou madest my arms a bronze bow.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Goliath’s challenge in the named heading
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source heading explicitly concerns Goliath; Samuel names Goliath and records his challenge to Israel for single combat. This identifies the named narrative figure without requiring every poetic battle image to be a literal detail of the encounter.

source_unit.text: Of David, concerning Goliath. Blessed is the Lord, my God, who trains my hands for battle array, my fingers for war.

target_units.text: A mighty man came out from the foreigners’ battle line, named Goliath, from Gath. His height was four cubits and a span.
A helmet was on his head, and he wore a coat of chain armour. His armour’s weight was five thousand shekels of bronze and iron.
Bronze greaves were on his legs, and a bronze shield was between his shoulders.
His spear’s shaft was like a weavers’ beam, and its iron head weighed six hundred shekels. The one carrying his weapons walked before him.

He stood and shouted to Israel’s battle line, “Why have you come out to draw up for war opposite us? Am I not a foreigner, and are you not Saul’s Hebrews? Choose a man for yourselves and let him come down to me.
If he can fight me and strike me down, we will become your slaves. But if I prevail and strike him down, you will become our slaves and serve us.”
The foreigner said, “Behold, I have defied Israel’s battle line today, on this day. Give me a man, and let the two of us fight in single combat.”

final_complete_triples.relationship: A cluster of divine refuge and rescue titles
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both lines call God the speaker’s refuge, helper, rescuer and protector or defender, and express hope in Him. Psalm 143’s subjecting of the people is a further clause, not part of this selected target.

source_unit.text: My mercy and my refuge, my Helper and my Rescuer, my Defender, in whom I hoped, who subjects my people beneath me.

target_units.text: The Lord is my firm foundation, my refuge, and my rescuer; my God is my helper, and I will hope in Him; my protector, the horn of my salvation, my supporter.

final_complete_triples.relationship: What is man or a son of man to God
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both questions pair man and son of man with God’s attention. Psalm 143 asks why God became known to him and takes account of him; Psalm 8 asks why He remembers and visits him.

source_unit.text: Lord, what is man, that Thou becamest known to him, or a son of man, that Thou takest account of him?

target_units.text: what is a human being, that Thou rememberest him, or a son of man, that Thou visitest him?

final_complete_triples.relationship: Human life passes like a shadow
final_complete_triples.rationale: The speaker likens a man to futility and his passing days to a shadow; Job describes the mortal’s short life as fleeing like a shadow. Job’s additional flower image is not imported into the psalm.

source_unit.text: A man was likened to futility; his days pass like a shadow.

target_units.text: “For a mortal born of woman is short-lived and full of wrath.
Like a flower that blossomed, he fell away; he fled like a shadow and will not remain.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Heaven bent down in a smoking divine descent
final_complete_triples.rationale: The request that the Lord bend heaven and descend, touching mountains so they smoke, corresponds to Psalm 17’s mountain shaking, smoke in divine anger and heaven bent in descent. The source’s touch is not asserted in the target.

source_unit.text: Lord, bend Thy heavens and descend; touch the mountains, and they will smoke.

target_units.text: And the earth was shaken and began to tremble; the foundations of the mountains were troubled and shaken because God was angry with them.
Smoke rose in His anger, and fire from His face set things ablaze; coals were kindled from Him.
And He bent heaven and came down, and gloom was beneath His feet.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Lightning and arrows scatter adversaries
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both lines combine divine lightning and arrows with scattering and throwing opponents into confusion. The request and expected action in Psalm 143 correspond to the narrated action of Psalm 17.

source_unit.text: Flash lightning, and Thou wilt scatter them; send out Thine arrows, and Thou wilt throw them into confusion.

target_units.text: And He sent out arrows and scattered them; He multiplied lightning flashes and threw them into turmoil.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Rescue from many waters from on high
final_complete_triples.rationale: The plea to send a hand from on high and take the speaker out of many waters closely corresponds to God sending from on high, taking the speaker and removing him from many waters.

source_unit.text: Send out Thy hand from on high; take me out and rescue me from many waters, from the hand of foreigners.

target_units.text: He sent from on high and took me; He took me to Himself out of many waters.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Same-chapter repetition of mouth and right-hand wrongdoing
final_complete_triples.rationale: This description of foreigners whose mouth spoke futility and whose right hand is a right hand of injustice returns in the later rescue petition. The exact repeated characterization links the petition to the previously described adversaries.

source_unit.text: Whose mouth spoke futility, and whose right hand is a right hand of injustice.

target_units.text: Rescue me and take me out from the hand of foreigners, whose mouth spoke futility and whose right hand is a right hand of injustice.

final_complete_triples.relationship: A new song with a ten-stringed psaltery
final_complete_triples.rationale: The promise of a new song and music on a ten-stringed psaltery corresponds to the paired commands for that instrument and a new song in Psalm 32.

source_unit.text: God, I will sing a new song unto Thee; on a ten-stringed psaltery I will make music unto Thee.

target_units.text: Give thanks to the Lord with the lyre; make music to Him with a ten-stringed psaltery.
Sing Him a new song; make music well with a shout of triumph.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Salvation of kings and David the servant
final_complete_triples.rationale: God’s saving kings and redeeming David His servant corresponds to magnifying His king’s salvations and showing mercy to His anointed, David. Psalm 143’s evil sword is not added to the target.

source_unit.text: To Him who gives salvation to kings, who redeems David His servant from an evil sword.

target_units.text: magnifying the salvations of His king and showing mercy to His anointed, to David and to his seed for ever.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Same-chapter return to rescue from the foreigner’s hand
final_complete_triples.rationale: The later petition repeats rescue from the foreigners’ hand and reproduces their mouth-and-right-hand description from the earlier two verses. This is an internal repeated plea rather than a second historical event.

source_unit.text: Rescue me and take me out from the hand of foreigners, whose mouth spoke futility and whose right hand is a right hand of injustice.

target_units.text: Send out Thy hand from on high; take me out and rescue me from many waters, from the hand of foreigners.
Whose mouth spoke futility, and whose right hand is a right hand of injustice.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Sons compared with young plants
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source compares their sons to young plants established in youth; Psalm 127 compares sons to newly planted olive trees around the table. The source’s whose remains attached to its own context, and neither household nor daughter imagery is equated with the target’s wife and children.

source_unit.text: Whose sons are like young plants established in their youth, their daughters beautified, adorned all around like the likeness of a sanctuary.

target_units.text: Your wife is like a flourishing vine in the sides of your house; your sons are like newly planted olive trees around your table.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Happiness of the people whose God is the Lord
final_complete_triples.rationale: The closing blessedness of the people whose God is the Lord closely corresponds to the blessed nation whose God is the Lord in Psalm 32. Psalm 143 distinguishes this from what they called happy in the preceding prosperity description.

source_unit.text: They called happy the people who have these things; happy the people whose God is the Lord.

target_units.text: Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, the people He chose as an inheritance for Himself.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Blessing the Lord’s name for ever
final_complete_triples.rationale: The speaker promises to bless God’s name for the age and age of the age; Psalm 112 blesses the Lord’s name from now and for ever. The royal address of Psalm 144 remains an additional feature.

source_unit.text: A praise of David. I will exalt Thee, my God, my King, and bless Thy name for the age and for the age of the age.

target_units.text: May the name of the Lord be blessed from now and for ever.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Continual blessing and praise
final_complete_triples.rationale: Blessing God every day and praising His name corresponds to blessing the Lord at every time and praise continually in the mouth. Both explicitly describe the ongoing practice, with different time expressions.

source_unit.text: Every day I will bless Thee and praise Thy name for the age and for the age of the age.

target_units.text: I will bless the Lord at every time; His praise is continually in my mouth.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The Lord great and greatly to be praised
final_complete_triples.rationale: The same declaration that the Lord is great and greatly to be praised occurs in both passages. Psalm 144 adds limitless greatness, while Psalm 95 adds fearfulness above all gods.

source_unit.text: Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised; His greatness has no limit.

target_units.text: For great is the Lord and greatly to be praised; He is fearsome above all gods.

final_complete_triples.relationship: God’s works and power told to successive generations
final_complete_triples.rationale: Generation praising God’s works and declaring His power to generation corresponds to announcing mighty acts and wonders so another generation and its children will know. The target gives the intergenerational teaching setting explicitly.

source_unit.text: Generation after generation will praise Thy works, and they will declare Thy power.

target_units.text: it was not hidden from their children for another generation, as we announce the Lord’s praises, His mighty acts and the wonders He did.
And He raised a testimony in Jacob and set a law in Israel, whatever He commanded our fathers to make known to their sons,
so that another generation might know, sons who will be born; and they will rise and announce it to their sons,

final_complete_triples.relationship: Declaring divine glory and wonders
final_complete_triples.rationale: Speech about the magnificence of God’s holy glory and recounting His wonders corresponds to the paired command to announce His glory and wonders among nations and peoples.

source_unit.text: They will speak of the magnificence of the glory of Thy holiness, and they will recount Thy wonders.

target_units.text: Announce His glory among the nations, His wonders among all the peoples.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Speaking of fearsome works and divine power
final_complete_triples.rationale: The declaration of God’s fearsome acts and greatness corresponds to the instruction to say to God how fearsome His works are, through the abundance of His power. The target’s enemies lying is not extended to the source.

source_unit.text: They will speak of the power of Thy fearsome acts, and they will recount Thy greatness.

target_units.text: Say to God, “How fearsome are Thy works! Through the abundance of Thy power, Thine enemies will lie unto Thee.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The abundance of divine kindness
final_complete_triples.rationale: Pouring forth remembrance of abundant kindness corresponds to the exclamation over the great multitude of the Lord’s kindness. Psalm 30 specifies those fearing and hoping in Him; Psalm 144 adds rejoicing in righteousness.

source_unit.text: They will pour forth remembrance of the abundance of Thy kindness and rejoice in Thy righteousness.

target_units.text: How great is the multitude of Thy kindness, Lord, which Thou didst conceal for those who fear Thee, which Thou didst accomplish for those who hope in Thee before the sons of men!

final_complete_triples.relationship: Compassionate and merciful, abundant in mercy
