final_complete_triples.rationale: The divine attributes compassionate, merciful and abundant in mercy closely parallel the proclamation in Exodus. The psalm says patient, while Exodus says slow to anger and adds true.

source_unit.text: Compassionate and merciful is the Lord, patient and abundant in mercy.

target_units.text: The Lord passed before him and proclaimed, “The Lord God, compassionate and merciful, slow to anger, abundant in mercy and true,

final_complete_triples.relationship: Mercy extending to all God’s works
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord’s kindness to all and compassion over all His works correspond to mercy on all and love for all existing things He made. The comparison follows the expressly universal scope of both passages.

source_unit.text: The Lord is kind to all, and His compassions are over all His works.

target_units.text: But Thou hast mercy on all, because Thou canst do all things, and Thou overlookest human sins with a view to repentance.
For Thou lovest all existing things and abhorrest nothing that Thou didst make; for Thou wouldst not have fashioned anything while hating it.
How could anything have endured unless Thou didst will it, or what had not been called by Thee have been preserved?
But Thou sparest all things, because they are Thine, Master who loves life.

final_complete_triples.relationship: All God’s works summoned to bless or thank Him
final_complete_triples.rationale: The summons for all God’s works to thank Him corresponds to all His works being told to bless Him throughout His dominion. Psalm 144 separately calls His holy ones to bless.

source_unit.text: Let all Thy works give thanks unto Thee, Lord, and let Thy holy ones bless Thee.

target_units.text: Bless the Lord, all His works, in every place of His dominion. Bless the Lord, my soul.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Making divine might known to people
final_complete_triples.rationale: Making God’s might known to the sons of men corresponds to the speaker’s desire to announce His arm and power to the coming generation. Psalm 144 further specifies the glorious kingdom.

source_unit.text: to make known to the sons of men Thy might and the glory of the magnificence of Thy kingdom.

target_units.text: And until old age and advanced years, God, do not forsake me, until I announce Thine arm to the whole coming generation, Thy power and Thy righteousness—

final_complete_triples.relationship: Everlasting dominion and an enduring kingdom
final_complete_triples.rationale: God’s kingdom of all ages and lordship through every generation correspond to the vision’s everlasting authority and kingdom never destroyed. The comparison concerns their explicit duration while preserving Daniel’s given-authority setting.

source_unit.text: Thy kingdom is a kingdom of all ages, and Thy lordship endures through every generation.

target_units.text: Authority was given him, and all the nations of the earth according to their families, and all glory, worshipped him. His authority is everlasting authority that will never be taken away, and his kingdom will never be destroyed.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Faithfulness in divine words and works
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord’s faithfulness in His words and holiness in His works correspond to the Lord’s upright word and all His works in faithfulness. The attributes are related but assigned differently in the two sentences.

source_unit.text: Faithful is the Lord in His words, and holy in all His works.

target_units.text: For the Lord’s word is upright, and all His works are in faithfulness.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The Lord raises the broken down
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source’s raising all who have been broken down closely repeats the Lord’s raising those broken down in Psalm 145. Psalm 144 additionally names support for the falling.

source_unit.text: The Lord supports all who are falling and raises up all who have been broken down.

target_units.text: The Lord raises up those broken down; the Lord makes the blind wise; the Lord loves the righteous.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Creatures wait for food at the right time
final_complete_triples.rationale: The eyes of all hoping in God and receiving food at the right time correspond to all waiting for Him to give food at the right time. The target’s creature context is read without limiting the source’s all to a different unstated group.

source_unit.text: The eyes of all hope in Thee, and Thou givest their food at the right time.

target_units.text: All wait for Thee to give them food at the right time.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The open divine hand fills living things
final_complete_triples.rationale: The open hand filling every living creature with good pleasure corresponds to God opening His hand and all things being filled with goodness. Good pleasure and goodness are preserved as the respective wording.

source_unit.text: Thou openest Thy hand and fillest every living creature with good pleasure.

target_units.text: When Thou givest to them, they will gather; when Thou openest Thy hand, all things will be filled with goodness.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Righteousness and holiness in God’s ways and works
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord’s righteousness in all His ways and holiness in all His works correspond to true works, ways that are judgments, and the declaration that the Lord is righteous and holy.

source_unit.text: The Lord is righteous in all His ways and holy in all His works.

target_units.text: God—true are His works, and all His ways are judgments; a faithful God, and there is no unrighteousness; righteous and holy is the Lord.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The Lord near when people call
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord’s nearness to those calling in truth corresponds to the rhetorical question about the Lord drawing near in all things in which His people call upon Him. The psalm’s truth qualification remains explicit.

source_unit.text: The Lord is near to all who call on Him, to all who call on Him in truth.

target_units.text: For what great nation is there whose god draws near unto them, as the Lord our God in all things wherein we call upon Him?

final_complete_triples.relationship: Hearing a plea and rescuing the faithful
final_complete_triples.rationale: God hearing the plea and saving those who fear Him corresponds to the righteous crying, the Lord hearing and rescuing them. The source also promises fulfillment of their will, which is not supplied to the target.

source_unit.text: He will fulfill the will of those who fear Him; He will hear their plea and save them.

target_units.text: The righteous cried out, and the Lord heard them; from all their afflictions He rescued them.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The Lord guards those who love Him
final_complete_triples.rationale: Guarding all who love the Lord corresponds to the address to those loving Him followed by His guarding the souls of His holy ones. The source destroys sinners; the target rescues the guarded people from sinners’ hands.

source_unit.text: The Lord guards all who love Him, and all sinners He will utterly destroy.

target_units.text: You who love the Lord, hate evil! The Lord guards the souls of His holy ones; He will rescue them from the hand of sinners.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Same-chapter closing return to blessing the name for ever
final_complete_triples.rationale: The final summons to bless God’s holy name for the age and age of the age returns to the opening promise to bless His name with the same duration. The close extends the speaker’s praise to all flesh.

source_unit.text: My mouth will speak the Lord’s praise, and let all flesh bless His holy name for the age and for the age of the age.

target_units.text: A praise of David. I will exalt Thee, my God, my King, and bless Thy name for the age and for the age of the age.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The soul summoned to praise or bless the Lord
final_complete_triples.rationale: Praise the Lord, my soul closely parallels Bless the Lord, my soul. The Haggai-and-Zechariah heading is preserved without using this verbal comparison to infer authorship.

source_unit.text: Hallelujah. Of Haggai and Zechariah. Praise the Lord, my soul.

target_units.text: Of David. Bless the Lord, my soul, and all that is within me, His holy name.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Lifelong praise and music as long as the speaker exists
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both speakers promise praise or singing throughout life and music to their God as long as they exist. The source’s praise and target’s sing are not treated as identical verbs.

source_unit.text: I will praise the Lord throughout my life; I will make music to my God as long as I exist.

target_units.text: I will sing to the Lord in my life; I will make music to my God as long as I exist.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Do not place trust in humans or rulers
final_complete_triples.rationale: The warning against trusting rulers and sons of men corresponds to the preference for trust and hope in the Lord over a man or rulers. Psalm 145 expressly grounds the warning in their lack of salvation.

source_unit.text: Do not trust in rulers and in sons of men who have no salvation.

target_units.text: Better to trust in the Lord than to trust in a man.
Better to hope in the Lord than to hope in rulers.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Departure of spirit and return to earth
final_complete_triples.rationale: The spirit going out and the person returning to his earth correspond to dust returning to earth and spirit returning to God. Ecclesiastes gives the spirit’s destination; the psalm adds the perishing of reasonings.

source_unit.text: His spirit will go out, and he will return to his earth; on that day all their reasonings will perish.

target_units.text: and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Jacob’s God as helper or supporter
final_complete_triples.rationale: The happiness of having Jacob’s God as helper corresponds to Jacob’s God being the community’s supporter. The individual hope and communal confession differ.

source_unit.text: Happy the one whose Helper is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the Lord his God,

target_units.text: The Lord of powers is with us; Jacob’s God is our supporter. Diapsalma.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Maker of heaven, earth, sea and their contents
final_complete_triples.rationale: The named creation of heaven, earth, sea and all in them closely corresponds to the same creation list in the Sabbath command. The psalm’s truth kept for ever and Exodus’ six days are distinct additional clauses.

source_unit.text: who made heaven and earth, the sea and all that is in them, who keeps truth for ever,

target_units.text: For in six days the Lord made heaven and earth and the sea and everything in them, and rested on the seventh day. Therefore the Lord blessed the seventh day and made it holy.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The Lord does judgment for the wronged
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord doing justice for those wronged corresponds closely to His deeds of mercy and judgment for all who are wronged. The source also feeds the hungry and releases prisoners.

source_unit.text: who does justice for those wronged, who gives food to the hungry. The Lord releases those in fetters.

target_units.text: The Lord does deeds of mercy and judgment for all who are wronged.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Release for those held captive
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord’s release of those in fetters corresponds to the commissioned speaker proclaiming release to captives. The Lord as releasing agent and His anointed messenger as proclaimer are distinguished.

source_unit.text: who does justice for those wronged, who gives food to the hungry. The Lord releases those in fetters.

target_units.text: The Lord’s spirit is upon me, because He anointed me. He sent me to bring good news to the poor, to heal the brokenhearted, to proclaim release to captives and recovery of sight to the blind,

final_complete_triples.relationship: Raising people who have been broken down
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord raising those broken down directly corresponds to Psalm 144’s raising all who have been broken down. The source’s making the blind wise is retained without changing it to the restoration of eyesight.

source_unit.text: The Lord raises up those broken down; the Lord makes the blind wise; the Lord loves the righteous.

target_units.text: The Lord supports all who are falling and raises up all who have been broken down.

final_complete_triples.relationship: God’s care for sojourner, orphan and widow
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord’s guarding newcomers and taking up orphan and widow corresponds to His judgment for sojourner, orphan and widow and love for the sojourner. Different descriptions of care remain distinct.

source_unit.text: The Lord guards the newcomers; He will take up the orphan and widow, and He will obliterate the way of sinners.

target_units.text: who executes judgment for the sojourner, and the orphan, and the widow, and loves the sojourner, to give him bread and clothing.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The Lord reigns for ever
final_complete_triples.rationale: The promise that the Lord will reign for ever corresponds to the song’s declaration that He reigns for ever and ever and beyond. Psalm 145 adds the address to Zion and every generation.

source_unit.text: The Lord will reign for ever, your God, Zion, through every generation.

target_units.text: The Lord reigns for ever and ever, and beyond.”

final_complete_triples.relationship: Goodness and beauty in the summons to praise
final_complete_triples.rationale: Psalm 146 commends praise because a psalm is good and asks that praise please God; Psalm 134 commands praise because the Lord is good and music because His name is beautiful. The differing subjects of good are preserved.

source_unit.text: Hallelujah. Of Haggai and Zechariah. Praise the Lord, for a psalm is good; may praise be pleasing to our God.

target_units.text: Praise the Lord, for the Lord is good; make music to His name, for it is beautiful.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Gathering Israel’s dispersed people
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord gathering Israel’s dispersed corresponds to His gathering Israel’s lost ones and Judah’s scattered ones from earth’s extremities. The building of Jerusalem is additional in the psalm.

source_unit.text: The Lord builds Jerusalem, and He will gather the dispersed of Israel.

target_units.text: He will raise a signal to the nations and gather Israel’s lost ones; He will gather Judah’s scattered ones from the earth’s four wings.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Healing the brokenhearted
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord healing the brokenhearted closely corresponds to the commissioned speaker sent to heal the brokenhearted. Binding fractures is additional in the psalm, and the agents are not confused.

source_unit.text: He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their fractures.

target_units.text: The Lord’s spirit is upon me, because He anointed me. He sent me to bring good news to the poor, to heal the brokenhearted, to proclaim release to captives and recovery of sight to the blind,

final_complete_triples.relationship: Numbering and naming the heavenly multitude
final_complete_triples.rationale: Numbering multitudes of stars and naming them corresponds to the heavenly array brought out by number and called by name. The psalm explicitly names stars; Isaiah’s upward-looking context supplies its heavenly setting.

source_unit.text: He numbers multitudes of stars and calls them all by names.

target_units.text: Lift your eyes on high and see: Who displayed all these? He brings out His array by number and will call all by name. From abundant glory and in strength’s might, nothing escaped you.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Divine understanding beyond measure or discovery
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord’s understanding beyond number corresponds to the Creator’s understanding that cannot be discovered. The comparison concerns the explicit limit of human measurement or discovery, not a claim that the terms are synonymous.

source_unit.text: Great is our Lord, and great is His strength; His understanding is beyond number.

target_units.text: And now, did you not know, if you have not heard? God is eternal, the God who fashioned the earth’s extremities. He will not hunger or grow weary, and His understanding cannot be discovered.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The Lord raises the lowly and brings low
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord taking up the meek and bringing sinners to the ground corresponds to His humbling and raising high, followed by lifting the needy from earth. The psalm identifies sinners as those brought low; Samuel’s selected statement does not.

source_unit.text: The Lord takes up the meek, but brings sinners low to the ground.

target_units.text: The Lord makes poor and makes rich; He humbles and raises high.
He raises the needy from the earth and lifts the poor from the dung heap, to seat them with rulers of peoples and grant them a throne of glory as their inheritance,

final_complete_triples.relationship: Thanksgiving with the lyre
final_complete_triples.rationale: The command to begin with thanksgiving and make music to God with a lyre closely corresponds to giving thanks to the Lord with a lyre. Psalm 32 additionally names a ten-stringed psaltery.

source_unit.text: Begin singing to the Lord with thanksgiving; make music to our God with a lyre,

target_units.text: Give thanks to the Lord with the lyre; make music to Him with a ten-stringed psaltery.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Rain, mountains, grass and growth for human service
final_complete_triples.rationale: Preparing rain and making grass sprout on mountains and green growth for humans corresponds to watering mountains and making grass and green plants spring up for livestock and human service.

source_unit.text: who clothes heaven with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who makes grass sprout on the mountains and green growth for the service of humans,

target_units.text: He waters mountains from His upper chambers; the earth will be filled with the fruit of Thy works.
He makes grass spring up for livestock and green plants for the service of humans, to bring bread out of the earth;

final_complete_triples.relationship: Food for young ravens calling to the Lord
final_complete_triples.rationale: God feeding young ravens calling upon Him corresponds to the question who prepared a raven’s food, with its nestlings crying to the Lord and seeking food. Cattle are an additional group in the psalm.

source_unit.text: who gives the cattle their food and to the young ravens who call upon Him.

target_units.text: Who prepared food for a raven? For its nestlings have cried to the Lord, wandering and seeking food.”

final_complete_triples.relationship: Horse and human strength contrasted with dependence on God
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord’s lack of delight in a horse’s might or human shins corresponds to the denial that great human force or a powerful horse saves. Divine pleasure and capacity to save are related contrasts, not the same assertion.

source_unit.text: He will not delight in the horse’s might, nor does He take pleasure in a man’s shins.

target_units.text: A king is not saved through a great force, and a giant will not be saved by the abundance of his strength.
A horse is false for salvation, and by the abundance of its power it will not be saved.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Those fearing God and hoping in His mercy
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord’s pleasure in those fearing Him and hoping in His mercy corresponds to His eyes being upon those described with the same paired expressions.

source_unit.text: The Lord takes pleasure in those who fear Him and in those who hope in His mercy.

target_units.text: Behold, the Lord’s eyes are upon those who fear Him, those who hope in His mercy,

final_complete_triples.relationship: Praise addressed from Zion and Jerusalem
final_complete_triples.rationale: Jerusalem and Zion are summoned to praise their God; Psalm 134 blesses the Lord from Zion and identifies His dwelling in Jerusalem. This compares the named city and its worship without dating the headings.

source_unit.text: Hallelujah. Of Haggai and Zechariah. Commend the Lord, Jerusalem; praise your God, Zion.

target_units.text: Blessed be the Lord from Zion, He who dwells in Jerusalem.

final_complete_triples.relationship: God feeds with the finest wheat
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord filling the city with the finest wheat closely corresponds to His feeding them with the finest wheat. The source’s peaceful borders and target’s honey are distinct additional provisions.

source_unit.text: He makes your borders peaceful and fills you with the finest wheat.

target_units.text: And He fed them with the finest wheat, and with honey from rock He satisfied them.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Snow and wool in paired imagery
final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm compares snow with wool, while Isaiah compares the whitening of sins with snow and wool. The shared pair supports a limited image comparison; mist like ashes and moral cleansing remain different subjects.

source_unit.text: of Him who gives snow like wool, who sprinkles mist like ashes,

target_units.text: Come, let us reason together, says the Lord. Though your sins are like purple-red, I will whiten them like snow; though they are like scarlet, I will whiten them like wool.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Ice and frost within divine rule over water
final_complete_triples.rationale: God casting ice like morsels and the question who withstands His cold correspond to Job’s questions about the origin of ice and frost and the fixing of the abyss’s face. The target’s actual flowing-water wording and questions are retained; it does not repeat the morsels image.

source_unit.text: who casts His ice like morsels; who will withstand His cold?

target_units.text: From whose belly does ice come forth, and who gave birth to frost in heaven,
which descends like flowing water? And who fixed the face of the abyss?

final_complete_triples.relationship: Divine breath or wind controls frost and water
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord’s sending His word to melt the ice and blowing wind so waters flow correspond to frost given from the Strong One’s breath and His steering water as He wishes. Frost-giving and melting are different actions.

source_unit.text: He will send His word and melt them; He will blow His wind, and waters will flow.

target_units.text: From the Strong One’s breath frost will be given, and He steers the water however He wishes.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Word and law declared to Jacob and Israel
final_complete_triples.rationale: God declaring His word, ordinances and judgments to Jacob and Israel corresponds to raising a testimony in Jacob and setting a law in Israel. The named people and divine instruction coincide, with distinct terms for that instruction.

source_unit.text: He declares His word to Jacob, His ordinances and judgments to Israel.

target_units.text: And He raised a testimony in Jacob and set a law in Israel, whatever He commanded our fathers to make known to their sons,

final_complete_triples.relationship: Israel’s distinctive divine judgments among nations
final_complete_triples.rationale: The claim that no other nation received this disclosure of judgments corresponds to the rhetorical question whether another great nation has such righteous ordinances and judgments. The comparison preserves the distinction between assertion and question.

source_unit.text: He did not do so for any nation, and He did not disclose His judgments to them.

target_units.text: For what great nation is there whose god draws near unto them, as the Lord our God in all things wherein we call upon Him?
And what great nation is there that has ordinances and judgments as righteous as all this law which I set before you this day?

final_complete_triples.relationship: The heavens summoned to praise
final_complete_triples.rationale: The summons to praise from the heavens and highest places corresponds to the summons for heavens and earth to praise. The target extends the range to sea and its creeping creatures.

source_unit.text: Hallelujah. Of Haggai and Zechariah. Praise the Lord from the heavens; praise Him in the highest places.

target_units.text: Let the heavens and earth praise Him, the sea and everything creeping in them.

final_complete_triples.relationship: All angels and powers summoned to worship
final_complete_triples.rationale: The paired summons to all God’s angels and powers to praise Him corresponds to the paired commands that all His angels and powers bless Him. Psalm 102 adds their doing His word and will.

source_unit.text: Praise Him, all His angels; praise Him, all His powers.

target_units.text: Bless the Lord, all His angels, mighty in strength, doing His word, so as to hear the voice of His words.
Bless the Lord, all His powers, His ministers who do His will.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The heavenly lights called to praise their maker
final_complete_triples.rationale: Sun, moon, stars and light are summoned within the psalm’s creation praise; Genesis describes the two great lights and stars set in heaven. The psalm’s named sun and moon are not substituted into Genesis’ wording.

source_unit.text: Praise Him, sun and moon; praise Him, all the stars and the light.

target_units.text: And God said, “Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven to give light upon the earth and to divide the day from the night. Let them serve for signs and seasons, for days and years.
And let them be lights in the firmament of heaven, to shine upon the earth.” And it was so.
And God made the two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night; He made the stars also.
And God set them in the firmament of heaven to shine upon the earth,
to rule the day and the night, and to divide the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Waters above heaven
final_complete_triples.rationale: The praise summons naming water above the heavens corresponds to the creation account’s water above the firmament, which God names Heaven. The heavens of heavens remain the psalm’s additional expression.

source_unit.text: Praise Him, heavens of heavens, and the water above the heavens.

target_units.text: And God said, “Let there be a firmament in the midst of the water, and let it divide water from water.” And it was so.
And God made the firmament, and God divided the water beneath the firmament from the water above the firmament.
And God called the firmament Heaven. And God saw that it was good. And there was evening, and there was morning: a second day.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Creation by divine speech and command
final_complete_triples.rationale: The reason for praise repeats the sequence that He spoke and they came to be, He commanded and they were created. This is a close verbal correspondence.

source_unit.text: Let them praise the Lord’s name, for He spoke, and they came to be; He commanded, and they were created.

target_units.text: For He spoke, and they came to be; He commanded, and they were created.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Creation endures under God’s established word
final_complete_triples.rationale: The enduring establishment and command that will not pass away correspond to God’s word remaining in heaven, the founded earth remaining, and all things serving His arrangement. The exact subjects and time expressions remain distinct.

source_unit.text: He established them for the age and for the age of the age; He set a command, and it will not pass away.

target_units.text: Twelve: Labd. For ever, Lord, Thy word remains in heaven.
Thy truth is from generation to generation; Thou didst found the earth, and it remains.
By Thine arrangement the day remains, for all things are Thy servants.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Earth and its watery realm summoned to praise
final_complete_triples.rationale: The summons from earth to dragons and deeps corresponds to heavens, earth, sea and everything creeping in them being summoned to praise. Dragons are not identified with a particular creature in the target.

source_unit.text: Praise the Lord from the earth, dragons and all deeps,

target_units.text: Let the heavens and earth praise Him, the sea and everything creeping in them.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Fire and wind in divine service
final_complete_triples.rationale: Fire and storm wind fulfilling God’s word can be compared with His angels as winds and ministers as burning fire. The relation is the explicit fire-and-wind service imagery, without deciding whether the two passages identify the same beings.

source_unit.text: fire, hail, snow, ice, storm wind—all fulfilling His word,

target_units.text: He makes His angels winds, and His ministers a burning fire.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Trees rejoicing or praising before the Lord
final_complete_triples.rationale: The summons to fruit trees and cedars to praise corresponds to all woodland trees exulting before the coming Lord. The psalm’s mountains and hills are not inserted into the target.

source_unit.text: mountains and all hills, fruit-bearing trees and all cedars,

target_units.text: The plains will rejoice, and everything in them; then all the trees of the woodland will exult
before the Lord, for He is coming, for He is coming to judge the earth. He will judge the inhabited world with righteousness and peoples with His truth.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Land creatures in creation and praise
final_complete_triples.rationale: The praise list of wild animals, cattle and creeping things corresponds to those kinds named in the creation of land animals. Winged birds are additional in the source, not in the selected target.

source_unit.text: wild animals and all cattle, creeping things and winged birds,

target_units.text: And God said, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kind: four-footed animals, creeping things, and wild beasts of the earth according to their kind.” And it was so.

And God made the wild beasts of the earth according to their kind, and the cattle according to their kind, and all the creeping things of the earth according to their kinds. And God saw that they were good.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Peoples and kingdoms assembled for the Lord’s praise
final_complete_triples.rationale: Earth’s kings, peoples, rulers and judges are summoned to praise; Psalm 101 joins the declaration of His praise to peoples and kingdoms gathering to serve Him. The target does not separately name judges.

source_unit.text: kings of the earth and all peoples, rulers and all judges of the earth,

target_units.text: to announce the Lord’s name in Zion and His praise in Jerusalem,
when peoples are gathered together, and kingdoms, to serve the Lord.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The Lord’s name and unique exaltation
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord’s name alone being exalted corresponds to the declaration that His name is Lord and He alone is Most High over all the earth. The source extends His praise over earth and heaven.

source_unit.text: Let them praise the Lord’s name, for His name alone was exalted; His praise is over earth and heaven.

target_units.text: and let them know that Thy name is Lord; Thou alone art Most High over all the earth.

final_complete_triples.relationship: A horn raised for God’s people or the righteous
final_complete_triples.rationale: Raising a horn of His people corresponds to the righteous person’s horns being raised alongside the promise to break sinners’ horns. The image is shared without identifying a particular ruler or event.

source_unit.text: He will raise a horn of His people— a hymn for all His holy ones, for the children of Israel, a people drawing near to Him.

target_units.text: And I will break together all sinners’ horns; and the righteous person’s horns will be raised.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The summons to sing a new song
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both passages command a new song to the Lord. Psalm 149 places praise in the assembly of holy ones; Psalm 95 summons all earth and includes a different heading.

source_unit.text: Hallelujah. Sing a new song to the Lord, His praise in the assembly of holy ones.

target_units.text: When the house was being built after the captivity; a song of David. Sing to the Lord a new song; sing to the Lord, all the earth.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Praise in the assembly of holy ones
final_complete_triples.rationale: Praise in the assembly of holy ones corresponds to acknowledgment of the Lord’s truth in an assembly of holy ones. The heavens are explicitly named in Psalm 88, without being inserted as the source assembly’s identity.

source_unit.text: Hallelujah. Sing a new song to the Lord, His praise in the assembly of holy ones.

target_units.text: The heavens will acknowledge Thy wonders, Lord, and Thy truth in an assembly of holy ones.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Israel’s maker and king
final_complete_triples.rationale: The summons for Israel to rejoice in its maker and Zion’s children in their king corresponds to the Lord who made and formed chosen Israel and identifies Himself as Israel’s King. The target’s Jacob address and womb imagery remain its own.

source_unit.text: Let Israel rejoice in the One who made it, and let Zion’s children exult in their King.

target_units.text: “But now listen, My servant Jacob, and Israel whom I chose.
Thus says the Lord God who made you and formed you from the womb: You will yet be helped. Do not fear, My servant Jacob and beloved Israel whom I chose.
For I will give water in thirst to those traveling through waterless land. I will place My spirit upon your offspring and My blessings upon your children,
and they will spring up like grass amid water and like a willow beside flowing water.
One will say, ‘I belong to God’; another will cry out in Jacob’s name; another will inscribe, ‘I belong to God,’ in Israel’s name.”
Thus says God, Israel’s King, who rescued him, God Sabaoth: “I am first, and I am after these things; apart from Me there is no God.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Timbrel and collective song to the Lord
final_complete_triples.rationale: Praising in a chorus with tambourine and psaltery can be compared with Miriam and the women using timbrels and dances as she leads the song to the Lord. Instruments, chorus and dancing are not treated as identical terms or one performance.

source_unit.text: Let them praise His name in a chorus; with tambourine and psaltery let them make music to Him.

target_units.text: Miriam the prophetess, Aaron’s sister, took a timbrel in her hand, and all the women went out after her with timbrels and dances.
And Miriam led them in song, saying, “Let us sing to the Lord, for He has been gloriously glorified; horse and rider He has cast into the sea.”

final_complete_triples.relationship: The meek lifted by the Lord
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord exalting the meek in salvation corresponds to His taking up the meek in Psalm 146. The source also states His pleasure in His people, and the target contrasts sinners brought low.

source_unit.text: For the Lord takes pleasure in His people, and He will exalt the meek in salvation.

target_units.text: The Lord takes up the meek, but brings sinners low to the ground.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Rejoicing and remembrance upon the bed
final_complete_triples.rationale: The holy ones rejoicing upon their beds can be compared with remembrance of God upon the speaker’s bed and exultation in the shelter of His wings. The target does not explicitly place all of its exultation on the bed.

source_unit.text: Holy ones will boast in glory and rejoice upon their beds.

target_units.text: If I remembered Thee upon my bed, in the dawn hours I meditated upon Thee.
For Thou becamest my helper, and in the shelter of Thy wings I will exult.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Two-edged swords in literal and comparative use
final_complete_triples.rationale: The holy ones hold two-edged swords while exalting God; Hebrews describes God’s word as sharper than any two-edged sword. The distinctive weapon expression is shared without making the psalm’s held swords a metaphor for the word.

source_unit.text: Exaltations of God in their throat, and two-edged swords in their hands,

target_units.text: For the word of God is living and active and sharper than any two-edged sword, penetrating as far as the division of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Vengeance and judgment upon enemies among nations
final_complete_triples.rationale: The purpose of executing vengeance and reproof among nations can be compared with the Lord’s declared repayment to enemies and vengeance for His sons’ blood. The psalm’s holy ones and Deuteronomy’s divine agent are distinguished; no specific written judgment is identified.

source_unit.text: to execute vengeance among the nations, reproofs among the peoples,

target_units.text: For I will sharpen My sword as lightning, and My hand shall lay hold of judgment; and I will repay a penalty unto the enemies, and unto them that hate Me will I repay.
I will make My arrows drunk with blood, and My sword shall devour flesh, from the blood of the slain and of captives, from the head of the rulers of the enemies.

Rejoice, O heavens, together with Him, and let all the sons of God worship Him; rejoice, O nations, with His people, and let all the angels of God give Him strength; for He avenges the blood of His sons, and shall avenge and repay a penalty unto the enemies, and unto them that hate Him shall He repay; and the Lord shall thoroughly cleanse the land of His people.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Kings subjected to judgment and fetters
final_complete_triples.rationale: The poetic binding of kings in fetters can be compared with the narrated judgment and fettering of King Sedekias. The historical captors are Babylonian, not identified as the psalm’s holy ones, and this is not asserted to fulfill the psalm.

source_unit.text: to bind their kings in fetters and their glorious ones in iron handcuffs,

target_units.text: They seized the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Deblatha, and he pronounced judgment upon him.
He slaughtered Sedekias’s sons before his eyes. He blinded Sedekias’s eyes, bound him with fetters, and brought him to Babylon.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Praise in heavenly and holy assembly language
final_complete_triples.rationale: Praise among God’s holy ones and in the firmament of His power corresponds to the heavens acknowledging His wonders and an assembly of holy ones acknowledging His truth. This does not resolve the identity of every holy one.

source_unit.text: Hallelujah. Praise God among His holy ones; praise Him in the firmament of His power.

target_units.text: The heavens will acknowledge Thy wonders, Lord, and Thy truth in an assembly of holy ones.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Praise according to greatness and mighty acts
final_complete_triples.rationale: Praise for mighty acts and abundant greatness corresponds to the Lord’s limitless greatness and the generations declaring His power and fearsome acts. The connection follows the explicit grounds for praise.

source_unit.text: Praise Him for His mighty acts; praise Him according to the abundance of His greatness.

target_units.text: Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised; His greatness has no limit.
Generation after generation will praise Thy works, and they will declare Thy power.
They will speak of the magnificence of the glory of Thy holiness, and they will recount Thy wonders.
They will speak of the power of Thy fearsome acts, and they will recount Thy greatness.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Trumpets and stringed instruments in praise
final_complete_triples.rationale: The summons to praise with trumpet, psaltery and lyre can be compared with appointed praise before the ark using harps, lyres and trumpets. The psaltery is not equated with every instrument name in Chronicles, and no performance date for the psalm is inferred.

source_unit.text: Praise Him with the sound of a trumpet; praise Him with psaltery and lyre.

target_units.text: He appointed some Levites to minister before the ark of the Lord’s covenant, to sound out, give thanks, and praise the Lord, Israel’s God:
Asaph the leader, Zacharias second to him, Jiiel, Semiramoth, Jiiel, Mattathias, Eliab, Banaias, Abdedom, and Jiiel, with instruments, harps, and lyres; Asaph sounded the cymbals.
Banaias and Oziel the priests sounded trumpets continually before the ark of God’s covenant.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Tambourine and chorus in praise
final_complete_triples.rationale: The summons to praise with tambourine and chorus closely corresponds to praising God’s name in a chorus and making music with tambourine and psaltery. Each passage retains its different additional instruments.

source_unit.text: Praise Him with tambourine and chorus; praise Him with strings and instrument.

target_units.text: Let them praise His name in a chorus; with tambourine and psaltery let them make music to Him.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Sounding cymbals in joyful praise
final_complete_triples.rationale: The command to praise with sounding cymbals corresponds to David’s appointment of singers and instruments to sound with gladness, including bronze cymbals. The source’s cymbals of a shout are not treated as a technical name found in Chronicles.

source_unit.text: Praise Him with well-sounding cymbals; praise Him with cymbals of a shout.

target_units.text: David said to the Levites’ rulers, “Appoint their brethren the psalm singers with song instruments—harps, lyres, and cymbals—to sound on high with a voice of gladness.”
The Levites appointed Aiman son of Joel; from his brethren, Asaph son of Barachia; and from Merari’s sons, his brethren, Aithan son of Kisaiou.
With them were their brethren of the second rank: Zacharias, Oziel, Semiramoth, Jiiel, Oni, Eliab, Banaia, Maasaia, Mattathia, Eliphalia, Makenia, Abdedom, Jiiel, and Ozias, the gatekeepers.
The psalm singers Aiman, Asaph, and Aithan were to make themselves heard with bronze cymbals.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The closing summons extends praise to all living voices
final_complete_triples.rationale: Let every breath praise the Lord corresponds to the closing summons for all flesh to bless His holy name. The collective scope and closing praise function are shared, while breath and flesh remain distinct expressions.

source_unit.text: Let every breath praise the Lord. Hallelujah.

target_units.text: My mouth will speak the Lord’s praise, and let all flesh bless His holy name for the age and for the age of the age.

final_complete_triples.relationship: David the youngest brother tending the flock
final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm’s small and younger David shepherding his father’s sheep corresponds to Jesse’s remaining youngest son tending the flock before being summoned. The narrative does not repeat every adjective in the psalm.

source_unit.text: This psalm is personally written concerning David and is outside the number, when he fought Goliath in single combat. I was small among my brothers and younger in my father’s house; I was shepherding my father’s sheep.

target_units.text: Jesse made his seven sons pass before Samuel. Samuel said, “The Lord has not chosen among these.”

Samuel said to Jesse, “Are these all the boys?” He said, “There is still the youngest; he is tending the flock.” Samuel said to Jesse, “Send and fetch him, for we will certainly not recline until he comes.”
He sent and brought him. He was ruddy, with beautiful eyes, and good to look upon before the Lord. The Lord said to Samuel, “Rise and anoint David, for this one is good.”

final_complete_triples.relationship: Goliath and the single-combat setting
final_complete_triples.rationale: The full heading places David’s fight with Goliath in single combat; Samuel identifies Goliath and records his challenge for two men to fight in single combat. The psalm’s outside-the-number statement remains its own heading metadata.

source_unit.text: This psalm is personally written concerning David and is outside the number, when he fought Goliath in single combat. I was small among my brothers and younger in my father’s house; I was shepherding my father’s sheep.

target_units.text: A mighty man came out from the foreigners’ battle line, named Goliath, from Gath. His height was four cubits and a span.
A helmet was on his head, and he wore a coat of chain armour. His armour’s weight was five thousand shekels of bronze and iron.
Bronze greaves were on his legs, and a bronze shield was between his shoulders.
His spear’s shaft was like a weavers’ beam, and its iron head weighed six hundred shekels. The one carrying his weapons walked before him.

He stood and shouted to Israel’s battle line, “Why have you come out to draw up for war opposite us? Am I not a foreigner, and are you not Saul’s Hebrews? Choose a man for yourselves and let him come down to me.
If he can fight me and strike me down, we will become your slaves. But if I prevail and strike him down, you will become our slaves and serve us.”
The foreigner said, “Behold, I have defied Israel’s battle line today, on this day. Give me a man, and let the two of us fight in single combat.”

final_complete_triples.relationship: David’s hands and musical instruments
final_complete_triples.rationale: David’s making an instrument and fitting a psaltery with his hands and fingers can be compared with his skill in playing and his hand playing the kinyra before Saul. Making and playing are different acts, and the instrument names are not equated.

source_unit.text: My hands made an instrument; my fingers fitted a psaltery.

target_units.text: One of his young servants answered, “I have seen a son of Jesse, a Beth-lehemite, skilled in playing. The man is discerning, a warrior, wise in speech, and good in appearance; the Lord is with him.”
Saul sent messengers to Jesse, saying, “Send me your son David, who is with your flock.”
Jesse took a gomor of loaves, a skin of wine, and one young goat, and sent them by the hand of his son David to Saul.
David came to Saul and stood before him. He loved him greatly, and he became the one carrying his equipment.
Saul sent to Jesse, saying, “Please let David stand before me, for he has found favour in my eyes.”
Whenever an evil spirit came upon Saul, David took the kinyra and played with his hand. Saul was refreshed, and it was well with him, and the evil spirit departed from him.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Questions about the Lord’s hearing
final_complete_triples.rationale: The assertion that the Lord Himself hears corresponds to the rhetorical question whether the One who planted the ear does not hear. This explains the shared hearing claim without assigning an unstated messenger to the source question.

source_unit.text: And who shall tell my Lord? He Himself is Lord; He Himself hears.

target_units.text: Does the One who planted the ear not hear, or the One who formed the eye not perceive?

final_complete_triples.relationship: David taken from the sheep and anointed
final_complete_triples.rationale: The account of being taken from the father’s sheep and anointed with oil corresponds to David summoned from the flock and anointed by Samuel. Psalm 151 names His angel while the Samuel narrative names Samuel; their identity is not resolved by the supported shepherd-to-anointing sequence.

source_unit.text: He Himself sent out His angel and took me from my father’s sheep and anointed me with the oil of His anointing.

target_units.text: Samuel said to Jesse, “Are these all the boys?” He said, “There is still the youngest; he is tending the flock.” Samuel said to Jesse, “Send and fetch him, for we will certainly not recline until he comes.”
He sent and brought him. He was ruddy, with beautiful eyes, and good to look upon before the Lord. The Lord said to Samuel, “Rise and anoint David, for this one is good.”
Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him among his brothers. The Lord’s Spirit leaped upon David from that day onward. Samuel rose and went to Armathaim.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Appearance does not secure the brothers’ election
final_complete_triples.rationale: The handsome and tall brothers in whom the Lord took no pleasure correspond to the warning not to regard Eliab’s appearance or height and the rejection of Jesse’s sons passing before Samuel. The narrative’s appearance warning is directed particularly at Eliab, not asserted of every brother.
